short_description: ABS controller auxiliary I/O channel 2 or 3 reads shorted high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 154 (ABS controller auxiliary I/O circuit) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the ABS/ESC on a configurable auxiliary output driver -- wired at the factory to a differential lock, transfer case, trailer, or a general-purpose 3/2 valve solenoid -- when that output circuit reads shorted to voltage or ground, open, or does not match its parameter-set configuration. Diagnosis follows the wiring for whichever solenoid the output is assigned to on this vehicle.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: ABS controller internal fault, diagnostic code CC
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 630 (Engine control module calibration/configuration fault) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the ABS/ESC for an internal fault -- a failed self-check, a lost link between the ECU's main and safety processing cores (or an add-on ESC module), a corrupted internal message, or another device-level condition the ECU cannot attribute to an external circuit. These are not driver-repairable; they are handled with a diagnostic tool and, if the fault repeats, ECU replacement.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: Wheel speed sensor, steer axle right, signal erratic
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 790 (Wheel speed sensor, steer axle right) with FMI 8 (Wrong frequency, pulse width or period) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed signal is plausible in amplitude but behaves erratically -- chattering, jumping, arriving at the wrong update rate, or disagreeing with the other wheels on the axle, including a sensor pair wired in reverse or an output too low at drive-off. Typical causes are a damaged or debris-packed tone ring, a loose sensor, mismatched tire sizes on an axle, or a mis-wired sensor after a service.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: Wheel speed sensor, additional axle left, signal lost
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 793 (Wheel speed sensor, additional axle left) with FMI 10 (Value changing implausibly fast or slow) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed signal is plausible in amplitude but behaves erratically -- chattering, jumping, arriving at the wrong update rate, or disagreeing with the other wheels on the axle, including a sensor pair wired in reverse or an output too low at drive-off. Typical causes are a damaged or debris-packed tone ring, a loose sensor, mismatched tire sizes on an axle, or a mis-wired sensor after a service.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: Pressure modulator valve, additional axle right, hold solenoid open circuit
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 800 (ABS pressure modulator valve channel, additional axle right) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the ABS/ESC when an ABS pressure-modulator valve solenoid circuit -- the hold or release coil, or the shared common return -- reads shorted, open, or has exceeded its expected duty-cycle life. The fault points to the solenoid coil, its wiring back to the ECU, or the modulator valve body itself.
source_doc: SD-13-4869 EC-60 ABS/ATC/ESP service data sheet (2013)

short_description: Pressure modulator valve, drive axle right, hold solenoid open circuit
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 935 (ABS modulator valve, drive axle right hold solenoid) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the ABS/ESC when an ABS pressure-modulator valve solenoid circuit -- the hold or release coil, or the shared common return -- reads shorted, open, or has exceeded its expected duty-cycle life. The fault points to the solenoid coil, its wiring back to the ECU, or the modulator valve body itself.
source_doc: SD-13-4983 EC-80 ABS/ATC service data sheet (2014)

short_description: Steering angle sensor calibration in progress
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1807 (Steering angle sensor (SAS) circuit) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the ABS/ESC when the steering-angle sensor (SAS) that feeds the stability control system reads out of range, times out on the data link, or has not finished its self-calibration. Causes range from a disconnected or misaligned sensor to a needed re-calibration after front-end or steering work.
source_doc: SD-13-4869 EC-60 ABS/ATC/ESP service data sheet (2013)

short_description: Fuel temperature reading moderately above normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 174 (Fuel temperature sensor) with FMI 16 (Moderately above normal range) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel temperature sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: 1200 Series marine auxiliary engines troubleshooting guide

short_description: Accelerator pedal idle validation circuit reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 91 (Accelerator pedal position sensor) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the accelerator pedal position sensor signal is missing, out of range or implausible relative to the engine's other timing references. Typical causes are a failed sensor, an incorrect air gap, connector corrosion, chafed wiring, or damage to the toothed wheel the sensor reads.
source_doc: A042J565 fire pump drive engine IOM, fault code charts

short_description: Engine coolant temperature sensor circuit reads high (shorted to supply)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 110 (Engine coolant temperature) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Engine ECU when the engine coolant temperature sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: Onan marine generator MDDCA operator manual

short_description: Transmission control module reports an implausible internal operation state
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 609 (Transmission control module internal operation fault) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Engine ECU when it detects an internal fault in its own memory, software or supply. Typical causes are a corrupted calibration, a power/ground fault at the ECU connector, or, rarely, a failed ECU that needs dealer replacement and reprogramming.
source_doc: A042J565 fire pump drive engine IOM, fault code charts

short_description: Injector solenoid, cylinder 4, circuit shorted to ground
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 654 (Injector cylinder 4) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel injector driver circuit reads an abnormal current, resistance or calibration value. Typical causes are a failed injector coil/solenoid, a chafed or corroded driver circuit, or an injector trim code that was not carried over after replacement.
source_doc: A042J565 fire pump drive engine IOM, fault code charts

short_description: Cylinder 3 exhaust temperature, left bank, far above normal
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1139 (Cylinder 3 exhaust temperature, left bank) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Engine ECU when the cylinder misfire/power-balance monitor fails to reach or hold the commanded position/pressure. Typical causes are a sticking or contaminated valve, a failed valve body, or an upstream system-pressure problem.
source_doc: A042J565 fire pump drive engine IOM, fault code charts

short_description: Cylinder 3 power, left bank, far above normal
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1325 (Misfire condition, cylinder 3) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Engine ECU when the cylinder misfire/power-balance monitor fails to reach or hold the commanded position/pressure. Typical causes are a sticking or contaminated valve, a failed valve body, or an upstream system-pressure problem.
source_doc: A042J565 fire pump drive engine IOM, fault code charts

short_description: Clutch actuator position sensor circuit shorted to ground, current too high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 33 (Clutch actuator position sensor) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Transmission when the Linear Clutch Actuator's position feedback or drive circuit reports an out-of-range, erratic, shorted or open condition, or the TECU cannot verify the clutch reached its commanded position. Typical causes are a worn or contaminated LCA position sensor, a failed actuator motor or drive circuit, a sticking clutch linkage, or a clutch touch-point calibration that has drifted out of limits.
source_page: Fault Code 250: Linear Clutch Actuator (LCA) Position Sensor
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Transmission air supply pressure reading moderately below the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 37 (Transmission air supply pressure) with FMI 18 (Moderately below normal range) is set by the Transmission when the shop-air supply pressure signal feeding the transmission's shift actuators leaves its plausible range, changes implausibly fast, or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. The Endurant's shift rails, clutch actuator and PTO solenoids all depend on this supply, so a genuine low-air condition (below roughly 100 psi at the TECU air pack) will also disrupt shifting.
source_page: Fault Code 215: Transmission Air Supply Pressure Sensor
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Transmission oil pressure reading below the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 127 (Transmission oil pressure) with FMI 1 (Reading in-range but far too low) is set by the Transmission when the transmission oil pressure signal reads below its plausible range, drifts, or the sensor circuit is open, shorted or out of calibration. Causes range from a failed pressure sensor to a genuine low-lubrication condition (low fluid, a clogged filter or a worn lube pump), which risks bearing and gear damage if not resolved.
source_page: Fault Code 210: Transmission Oil Pressure (Fluid Pressure Sensor)
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Transmission countershaft speed value drifting downward over time
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 160 (Transmission countershaft speed) with FMI 21 (Value has drifted downward over time) is set by the Transmission when the countershaft speed sensor signal is erratic, out of frequency, drifting, below its plausible range, or reads an open/shorted circuit. This sensor is used for clutchless shift timing and synchronizer protection.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Transmission oil temperature circuit shorted to ground, current too high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 177 (Transmission oil temperature) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Transmission when the transmission fluid temperature signal leaves its plausible window, changes implausibly fast, or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Causes range from a failed thermistor or chafed harness to a genuine overheating condition (low fluid, a restricted cooler or heavy duty cycle).
source_page: Fault Code 212: Transmission Oil Temperature (Fluid Temperature Sensor)
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Transmission output shaft speed value drifting upward over time
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 191 (Transmission output shaft speed) with FMI 20 (Value has drifted upward over time) is set by the Transmission when the output shaft speed sensor signal is erratic, out of frequency, drifting, reads an open/shorted circuit, or the TECU cannot determine a plausible value from it. This sensor is used for road speed and shift confirmation.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Driveline engagement status: signal erratic or implausible
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 560 (Driveline engagement status) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Transmission when it cannot confirm the clutch or the overall driveline reached the engagement state it commanded, or the confirmation logic behaves erratically or drifts from the expected timing. This points to a genuine mechanical engagement problem (slipping clutch, worn synchronizers, low actuation pressure) rather than a single sensor fault, so treat it as a system-level confirmation issue.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Road grade (incline) sensor stored calibration values are out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 583 (Road grade (incline) sensor) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Transmission when the grade/inclination sensor used for grade-based shift scheduling reads erratic, out of frequency, changing implausibly fast, drifting, a device or calibration fault, or its value arrives flagged as a network error. The TECU diagnoses this sensor directly rather than only relaying it, so mounting/orientation and calibration are in scope alongside the wiring and network checks.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Transmission control module internal operation fault not reported at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 609 (Transmission control module internal operation fault) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is an internal TECU self-check or watchdog fault, set when the module's own operation is outside its expected range, timing or state. It is not tied to a single external circuit, so rule out power, ground and network faults first before treating it as a module problem.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Engine control unit internal fault logged with no further diagnostic detail available
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 629 (Engine control unit internal fault) with FMI 31 (Fault present; no further detail) is an internal TECU self-check or watchdog fault, set when the module's own operation is outside its expected range, timing or state. It is not tied to a single external circuit, so rule out power, ground and network faults first before treating it as a module problem.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Secondary shift device signal circuit voltage low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 752 (Secondary shift device signal) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Transmission when the shift lever or multiplexed shift-selector device reports an electrical fault, an implausible or erratic signal, or a message that is not arriving at the expected rate.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail E, fore solenoid circuit current moderately above the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 768 (Shift rail E, fore solenoid) with FMI 16 (Moderately above normal range) is set by the Transmission when one of the X-Y shift rail fore/aft solenoids reads an electrical fault (open, short, out-of-range) or fails to move the rail as commanded, preventing the TECU from selecting or confirming the requested gear.
source_page: Fault Code 646: Rail E Fore Solenoid (A6)
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Transmission inertia brake solenoid not moving to the commanded position
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 787 (Transmission inertia brake solenoid) with FMI 7 (Mechanical part not reacting or misadjusted) is set by the Transmission when the driveline inertia brake solenoid, used to slow the countershaft for clutchless upshifts, reads an electrical fault, an out-of-range response, or fails a calibration check.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Rear axle 1, right wheel speed sensor stored calibration values are out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 908 (Rear axle 1, right wheel speed sensor) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Transmission when a value the brake or ABS/ESC system broadcasts on J1939 -- a wheel speed, a brake pressure, a brake/hill-holder switch state, ABS/ASR status, or an external brake request (XBR) -- stops arriving at the expected rate, fails validation, or is out of the receiving controller's calibrated range. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than measuring it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the brake/ABS system's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ABS/ESC controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.
source_page: Fault Code 193: Rear Axle 1 Right Wheel Speed
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Engine default torque limit reported by the module as internally defective
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1846 (Engine default torque limit) with FMI 12 (Smart device or component defective) is set by the Transmission when a value the engine control system broadcasts on J1939 -- engine speed, torque, accelerator pedal position, an idle/torque limit, or an engine configuration message -- stops arriving at the expected rate, fails validation, or is out of the receiving controller's calibrated range. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than measuring it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the engine ECU's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the engine ECU for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.
source_page: Fault Code 174: Engine Default Torque Limit
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: PTO 1 request signal reported by the module as internally defective
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3452 (PTO 1 request signal) with FMI 12 (Smart device or component defective) is set by the Transmission when the driver's PTO request input (a dash switch or multiplexed request) reads a circuit fault, a calibration issue, or a message that is not arriving at the expected rate.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: PTO 1 engage signal circuit shorted to ground, current too high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3456 (PTO 1 engage signal) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Transmission when the PTO engagement air solenoid reads an electrical fault (open, short, out-of-range) or the PTO fails to mechanically engage as commanded.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: PTO 1 engagement confirmation message not received at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3460 (PTO 1 engagement confirmation) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Transmission when the sensor/switch that confirms the PTO has actually engaged reports a circuit fault, a drifting calibration, a message that is not arriving at the expected rate, or a mechanical condition where the PTO never reaches the confirmed position.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) signal message not received at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3651 (Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) signal) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Transmission when a value from the cruise control or Automated Driving System (ADS) stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation -- a primary/secondary ADS command, an ADS operation-status report, or a cruise resume/pause command. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than generating it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the sending controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ADS/cruise source controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Transmission secondary shift-down selector signal erratic or implausible
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3656 (Transmission secondary shift-down selector) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Transmission when the shift lever or multiplexed shift-selector device reports an electrical fault, an implausible or erratic signal, or a message that is not arriving at the expected rate.
source_page: Fault Code 144: Transmission Secondary Shift Down Selector
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Two-speed axle switch stored calibration values are out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4056 (Two-speed axle switch) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Transmission when the driver's two-speed axle range switch, routed through the TECU, reads a circuit fault, a calibration issue, or the confirmation status message the TECU reports for it is not arriving at the expected rate.
source_page: Fault Code 986: Two Speed Axle Switch
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail A position sensor message not received at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4218 (Shift rail A position sensor) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail position sensor reads out of range, erratic, drifting, or an open/shorted circuit, so the TECU cannot confirm which rail position (gear) is actually selected.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Clutch engage solenoid 1 drive current's rate of change outside plausible limits
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5614 (Clutch engage solenoid 1) with FMI 10 (Value changing implausibly fast or slow) is set by the Transmission when one of the clutch engage or release solenoids reads an open circuit, a short to power or ground, an out-of-range coil resistance, or fails to respond at the commanded frequency. These solenoids meter shop air to the clutch actuator, so an electrical fault here directly stops clutch engagement or release.

These solenoids meter shop air to the clutch actuator, so an electrical fault here directly stops clutch engagement or release.

detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5941 (Shift rail D position sensor) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail position sensor reads out of range, erratic, drifting, or an open/shorted circuit, so the TECU cannot confirm which rail position (gear) is actually selected.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail E position sensor circuit voltage high (shorted to supply)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5942 (Shift rail E position sensor) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail position sensor reads out of range, erratic, drifting, or an open/shorted circuit, so the TECU cannot confirm which rail position (gear) is actually selected.
source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail D calibration procedure not completing or producing an implausible value
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5954 (Shift rail D calibration) with FMI 7 (Mechanical part not reacting or misadjusted) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail's stored calibration end-points have drifted out of limits, or a mechanical condition prevents the rail from completing its calibration stroke.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail B operation status: reading moderately below the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 6145 (Shift rail B operation status) with FMI 18 (Moderately below normal range) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail does not reach or hold the commanded position within the expected time or range, indicating a mechanical shift-quality problem (binding synchronizer, worn shift fork, low air pressure) rather than a wiring fault.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Shift rail D operation status: reading slightly above the normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 6147 (Shift rail D operation status) with FMI 15 (Slightly above normal range) is set by the Transmission when a shift rail does not reach or hold the commanded position within the expected time or range, indicating a mechanical shift-quality problem (binding synchronizer, worn shift fork, low air pressure) rather than a wiring fault.
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Transmission clutch operation status: flagged under a manufacturer-specific fault condition
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 6150 (Transmission clutch operation status) with FMI 14 (See manufacturer-specific instructions) is set by the Transmission when the Linear Clutch Actuator's position feedback or drive circuit reports an out-of-range, erratic, shorted or open condition, or the TECU cannot verify the clutch reached its commanded position. short_description: Force-hold neutral input signal frequency, pulse width or period abnormal
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 7695 (Force-hold neutral input signal) with FMI 8 (Wrong frequency, pulse width or period) is set by the Transmission when the driver-operated force-hold-neutral input or output (used to hold the transmission in neutral, for example during PTO operation) reads an electrical fault, a calibration issue, or a message that is not arriving at the expected rate.

source_doc: TRTS0960 Endurant XD fault code index

short_description: TSC1 control message source address (purpose P7) message not received at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 11756 (TSC1 control message source address (purpose P7)) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Transmission when it cannot determine which physical node on the J1939 network is entitled to send a given command -- the controlling device's source address is unconfigured, is not the address the Transmission expects, or is being claimed by more than one node at once. Typical causes are a recently swapped or reprogrammed ECU that never had its source address set, two nodes with the same factory-default address, or a parameter file mismatch after an aftermarket device was added to the network.
source_page: Fault Code 137: Source Address of Controlling Device for TSC1 Control Purpose P7
source_doc: TRTS0950 Endurant HD fault code index

short_description: Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) operation status: message not received at the expected rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 20870 (Primary automatic drive selector (ADS) operation status) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Transmission when a value from the cruise control or Automated Driving System (ADS) stops arriving at the expected rate or fails validation -- a primary/secondary ADS command, an ADS operation-status report, or a cruise resume/pause command. The Transmission only receives this value over the network rather than generating it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the sending controller's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ADS/cruise source controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Transmission itself has failed.

detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 94 (Fuel delivery pressure sensor) with FMI 16 (Moderately above normal range) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel delivery (low-side) pressure sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.

short_description: Air filter restriction sensor, reading far too high (most severe)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 107 (Air filter restriction sensor) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Engine ECU when the intake air filter shows excessive restriction or an abnormal differential-pressure reading. Typical causes are a filter past its service interval, an abnormal contamination source, or a failed differential-pressure sensor.
source_doc: OMRG35856 PowerTech DTC list

short_description: Engine speed (RPM) signal, moderately below normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 190 (Engine speed (RPM) signal) with FMI 18 (Moderately below normal range) is set by the Engine ECU when the engine speed (overspeed protection) monitor signal is missing, erratic or implausible. Typical causes are a failed sensor, an incorrect air gap, chafed wiring, or damage to the tone wheel/reluctor the sensor reads.
source_doc: OMRG35856 PowerTech DTC list

short_description: Engine camshaft/timing position sensor signal, missing or wrong frequency
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 637 (Engine camshaft/timing position sensor signal) with FMI 8 (Wrong frequency, pulse width or period) is set by the Engine ECU when the crankshaft or camshaft position sensor signal is missing, out of range or implausible relative to the engine's other timing references. Typical causes are a failed sensor, an incorrect air gap, connector corrosion, chafed wiring, or damage to the toothed wheel the sensor reads.
source_doc: OMRG35856 PowerTech DTC list

short_description: Injector cylinder 4, open circuit (current too low)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 654 (Injector cylinder 4) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel injector driver circuit reads an abnormal current, resistance or calibration value. Typical causes are a failed injector coil/solenoid, a chafed or corroded driver circuit, or an injector trim code that was not carried over after replacement.
source_doc: OMH229936 9670/9770 STS engine control unit DTCs

short_description: Electric fuel lift pump relay/circuit, shorted to ground (current too high)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1075 (Electric fuel lift pump relay/circuit) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel supply (transfer) pump circuit or its commanded response is abnormal. Typical causes are a failed coil/solenoid, corroded or chafed wiring, or the actuator mechanically sticking.
source_doc: OMRG35856 PowerTech DTC list

short_description: EGR fresh air (inlet) temperature sensor, moderately above normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2630 (EGR fresh air (inlet) temperature sensor) with FMI 16 (Moderately above normal range) is set by the Engine ECU when the pressure differential across the EGR circuit (or the fresh-air temperature downstream of the EGR cooler) is implausible or high. A fouled or internally leaking EGR cooler, a plugged EGR orifice, or a genuine differential pressure sensor fault are the usual causes.
source_doc: OMH229936 9670/9770 STS engine control unit DTCs

short_description: EGR valve 2 position sensor, calibration data invalid
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3822 (EGR valve 2 position sensor) with FMI 13 (Calibration data outside limits) is set by the Engine ECU when the EGR valve actuator will not reach or hold a commanded position, reports an internal fault, loses calibration, or the motor coil circuit is open or shorted. Carbon buildup in the valve bore that increases actuator load is a leading mechanical cause behind an electrical-looking fault.
source_doc: OMH229936 9670/9770 STS engine control unit DTCs

short_description: Electronic gauge cluster, tachometer sensor fault is not being received at the expected message rate
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2023 (Electronic gauge cluster, tachometer sensor fault) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the Body controller when the gauge cluster -- or one gauge within it, such as the tachometer -- is not receiving the J1939-broadcast data it is meant to display, either because the source message has timed out or because the cluster itself has flagged an internal fault and fallen back to a default display. Typical causes are a connector or wiring fault between the cluster and the backbone, the sending controller going silent, or a faulted cluster module.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Door lock status signal is not responding to the commanded position
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3415 (Door lock status signal) with FMI 7 (Mechanical part not reacting or misadjusted) is set by the Body controller when a power door lock or latch actuator does not reach its commanded position, or the actuator's status/tell-tale circuit reads open or shorted. Typical causes are a mechanically binding or frozen lock mechanism, a failed door lock actuator, or a corroded connector or damaged wiring in the door harness.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Transfer case status (general fault) is open, no current detected
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4046 (Transfer case status (general fault)) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the Body controller when a power take-off, transfer case, or driveline engagement sensor or solenoid circuit interfaced through the body controller reads open, shorted, or erratic. Typical causes are a failed position sensor or engagement solenoid, a corroded connector at the PTO or transfer case, or damaged wiring between the component and the body controller.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Remote power module 2, channel 5 output does not match the commanded state
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520488 (Remote power module 2, channel 5 output) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Body controller when a Remote Power Module (RPM) output channel reports a state the ESC does not expect for the load configured on that channel — open, shorted to ground, or not updating. Typical causes are a failed load device, a corroded connector at the RPM or the load, or damaged wiring on that channel's circuit.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: TEM auxiliary 1 interlock switch input is erratic or not read correctly
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520552 (TEM auxiliary 1 interlock switch input) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Body controller when a multiplexed switch pack module stops reporting valid switch states to the ESC, and the ESC defaults every switch in that pack to its fallback value. Typical causes are a failed or unpowered switch pack module, a corroded or unseated connector at the module, or damaged wiring on the multiplex link between the switch pack and the body controller.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: TEM dual switch 1 input is erratic or not read correctly
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520589 (TEM dual switch 1 input) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Body controller when a multiplexed switch pack module stops reporting valid switch states to the ESC, and the ESC defaults every switch in that pack to its fallback value. Typical causes are a failed or unpowered switch pack module, a corroded or unseated connector at the module, or damaged wiring on the multiplex link between the switch pack and the body controller.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Front driveline engagement circuit is open, no current detected
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520734 (Front driveline engagement circuit) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the Body controller when a power take-off, transfer case, or driveline engagement sensor or solenoid circuit interfaced through the body controller reads open, shorted, or erratic. Typical causes are a failed position sensor or engagement solenoid, a corroded connector at the PTO or transfer case, or damaged wiring between the component and the body controller.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Blackout lighting ignition relay 1 circuit is shorted to ground or drawing excess current
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520871 (Blackout lighting ignition relay 1 circuit) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Body controller when a blackout-drive, convoy, or trailer blackout lamp output circuit reads shorted to ground rather than the expected lamp load. This equipment is fitted on tactical and convoy-configured vocational trucks; typical causes are a failed blackout lamp assembly, water intrusion at the lamp connector, or chafed wiring in the trailer or chassis harness feeding the blackout circuit.
source_doc: S08327 Body Controller Diagnostic Trouble Codes (2010)

short_description: Engine coolant temperature sensor signal stuck, not responding to changes
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 110 (Engine coolant temperature) with FMI 31 (Fault present; no further detail) is set by the Engine ECU when the engine coolant temperature sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: Cylinder 3 injector circuit reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 653 (Injector cylinder 3) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel injector driver circuit reads an abnormal current, resistance or calibration value. Typical causes are a failed injector coil/solenoid, a chafed or corroded driver circuit, or an injector trim code that was not carried over after replacement.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: Ignition coil H primary circuit open (no current)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1270 (Ignition coil H primary circuit) with FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) is set by the Engine ECU when the ignition coil circuit or its commanded response is abnormal. Typical causes are a failed coil/solenoid, corroded or chafed wiring, or the actuator mechanically sticking.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: ABS control module message failed checksum validation
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2011 (Loss/invalid data from ABS control module) with FMI 19 (Network-received value flagged as error) is set by the Engine ECU when a value the brake or ABS/ESC system broadcasts on J1939 -- a wheel speed, a brake pressure, a brake/hill-holder switch state, ABS/ASR status, or an external brake request (XBR) -- stops arriving at the expected rate, fails validation, or is out of the receiving controller's calibrated range. The Engine ECU only receives this value over the network rather than measuring it directly, so the fault is a link problem until the brake/ABS system's own diagnostics say otherwise: check the ABS/ESC controller for its own active codes and confirm it is still transmitting before assuming the Engine ECU itself has failed.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: Oxygen sensor heater circuit, bank 2 sensor 1, reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3262 (Oxygen sensor heater circuit, bank 2 sensor 1) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU for the lambda (wideband O2) sensor used to trim the aftertreatment/combustion feedback loop, or for a post-catalyst fuel trim that has moved outside its expected band. A lazy or contaminated sensor and an exhaust leak ahead of the sensor are the most common causes on gasoline- and dual-fuel heavy-duty engines with a three-way or oxidation catalyst.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: Oxygen sensor, bank 2 sensor 1, switches from rich to lean too slowly
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 4241 (Oxygen sensor response time, bank 2 sensor 1) with FMI 10 (Value changing implausibly fast or slow) is set by the Engine ECU for the lambda (wideband O2) sensor used to trim the aftertreatment/combustion feedback loop, or for a post-catalyst fuel trim that has moved outside its expected band. A lazy or contaminated sensor and an exhaust leak ahead of the sensor are the most common causes on gasoline- and dual-fuel heavy-duty engines with a three-way or oxidation catalyst.
source_doc: PSI 6.0L OBD-HD engine diagnostic manual (FCCC chassis)

short_description: Secondary accelerator pedal position sensor frequency or pulse width out of range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 29 (Secondary accelerator pedal position sensor) with FMI 8 (Wrong frequency, pulse width or period) is set by the Engine ECU when the accelerator pedal position sensor signal is missing, out of range or implausible relative to the engine's other timing references. Typical causes are a failed sensor, an incorrect air gap, connector corrosion, chafed wiring, or damage to the toothed wheel the sensor reads.
source_doc: SEBU8601-07 1206E-E70TTA industrial engine OMM, Table 3 diagnostic codes

short_description: Fuel temperature sensor circuit reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 174 (Fuel temperature sensor) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel temperature sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: SEBU8601-07 1206E-E70TTA industrial engine OMM, Table 3 diagnostic codes

short_description: Common rail (fuel) pressure sensor reading far above normal range
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1239 (Common rail (fuel) pressure sensor) with FMI 0 (Reading in-range but far too high) is set by the Engine ECU when the fuel rail (common rail) pressure sensor signal leaves its plausible window or the sensor circuit reads open, shorted or erratic. Typical causes are a failed sensor, corroded connector pins, chafed harness wiring, or a genuine underlying system condition the sensor is correctly reporting.
source_doc: SEBU8601-07 1206E-E70TTA industrial engine OMM, Table 3 diagnostic codes

short_description: ECU sensor supply voltage 2 circuit reads high (shorted to supply)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3510 (ECU sensor supply voltage 2, out-of-range fault) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Engine ECU when the 5V/8V sensor supply rail reads outside its expected voltage band. Typical causes are a shorted sensor or harness branch overloading the shared supply, a corroded connector, or a failed regulator/relay.
source_doc: SEBU8601-07 1206E-E70TTA industrial engine OMM, Table 3 diagnostic codes

short_description: Parameter 5425: circuit current too low (open circuit)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 5425 (Parameter 5425 (role not stated by the OEM tables)) is a Perkins-specific parameter with no plain-language description in the source OEM tables; FMI 5 (Current too low; open circuit) reported by the Engine ECU indicates a circuit-type electrical fault (open, short or out-of-range voltage) on whatever sensor or actuator this parameter represents. Diagnose it as a wiring/connector fault using the OEM pin-out for this SPN rather than assuming a specific component.
source_doc: SEBU8601-07 1206E-E70TTA industrial engine OMM, Table 3 diagnostic codes

short_description: Trailer auxiliary output circuit (WABCO aux): circuit shorted to ground (voltage low)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 704 (Auxiliary I/O channel 4) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the ABS/ESC on a configurable auxiliary output driver -- wired at the factory to a differential lock, transfer case, trailer, or a general-purpose 3/2 valve solenoid -- when that output circuit reads shorted to voltage or ground, open, or does not match its parameter-set configuration. Diagnosis follows the wiring for whichever solenoid the output is assigned to on this vehicle.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: Wheel speed sensor, steer axle right: signal frequency or pulse width wrong
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 790 (Wheel speed sensor, steer axle right) with FMI 8 (Wrong frequency, pulse width or period) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed signal is plausible in amplitude but behaves erratically -- chattering, jumping, arriving at the wrong update rate, or disagreeing with the other wheels on the axle, including a sensor pair wired in reverse or an output too low at drive-off. Typical causes are a damaged or debris-packed tone ring, a loose sensor, mismatched tire sizes on an axle, or a mis-wired sensor after a service.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: Sensor circuit shorted; check for corroded or damaged wiring (drive axle right)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 792 (Wheel speed sensor, drive axle right) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed sensor circuit reads open, shorted to voltage or ground, or the sensor no longer reports as a valid device to the ECU. Typical causes are a broken or corroded sensor connector, a chafed harness near the axle or suspension travel, a failed sensor coil, or a wiring short at the ECU pin.
source_doc: MM0112 ABS/ESC E-version maintenance manual (05.2020)

short_description: Wheel speed sensor, additional axle right: circuit shorted to ground, current too high
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 794 (Wheel speed sensor, additional axle right) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed sensor circuit reads open, shorted to voltage or ground, or the sensor no longer reports as a valid device to the ECU. Typical causes are a broken or corroded sensor connector, a chafed harness near the axle or suspension travel, a failed sensor coil, or a wiring short at the ECU pin.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: ABS pressure modulator valve channel, additional axle right: circuit shorted to ground (voltage low)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 800 (ABS pressure modulator valve channel, additional axle right) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the ABS/ESC when an ABS pressure-modulator valve solenoid circuit -- the hold or release coil, or the shared common return -- reads shorted, open, or has exceeded its expected duty-cycle life. The fault points to the solenoid coil, its wiring back to the ECU, or the modulator valve body itself.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: ESC disabled; steering ratio implausible, recalibrate SAS after steering/front-axle work
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 1807 (Steering angle sensor (SAS) circuit) with FMI 7 (Mechanical part not reacting or misadjusted) is set by the ABS/ESC when the steering-angle sensor (SAS) that feeds the stability control system reads out of range, times out on the data link, or has not finished its self-calibration. Causes range from a disconnected or misaligned sensor to a needed re-calibration after front-end or steering work.
source_doc: MM0112 ABS/ESC E-version maintenance manual (05.2020)

short_description: ESC module CAN communication fault: message counter increments incorrectly
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520210 (ESC module CAN communication fault) with FMI 8 (Wrong frequency, pulse width or period) is set by the ABS/ESC when the primary or secondary J1939 vehicle network is reporting a general fault -- traffic that is erratic, arriving too slowly, or a multiplexing/configuration mismatch -- that is not tied to one identifiable partner message. Typical causes are marginal wiring shared with the physical-layer fault list, a node flooding or slowing the bus, a baud-rate or address mismatch after a software update, or (on older engine ECUs) a fault on the legacy J1587 serial link that still runs alongside J1939.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: Wheel-speed plausibility, axle 2 right: sudden downward jump in wheel-speed reading
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520504 (Wheel-speed plausibility, axle 2 right) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed signal is plausible in amplitude but behaves erratically -- chattering, jumping, arriving at the wrong update rate, or disagreeing with the other wheels on the axle, including a sensor pair wired in reverse or an output too low at drive-off. Typical causes are a damaged or debris-packed tone ring, a loose sensor, mismatched tire sizes on an axle, or a mis-wired sensor after a service.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: Wheel-speed plausibility, axle 6 left: no wheel-speed signal being measured for this wheel
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520511 (Wheel-speed plausibility, axle 6 left) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the ABS/ESC when a wheel-speed signal is plausible in amplitude but behaves erratically -- chattering, jumping, arriving at the wrong update rate, or disagreeing with the other wheels on the axle, including a sensor pair wired in reverse or an output too low at drive-off. Typical causes are a damaged or debris-packed tone ring, a loose sensor, mismatched tire sizes on an axle, or a mis-wired sensor after a service.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: Auxiliary output solenoid ground circuit: shorted to supply (voltage high)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 520523 (Auxiliary output solenoid ground circuit) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the ABS/ESC on a configurable auxiliary output driver -- wired at the factory to a differential lock, transfer case, trailer, or a general-purpose 3/2 valve solenoid -- when that output circuit reads shorted to voltage or ground, open, or does not match its parameter-set configuration. Diagnosis follows the wiring for whichever solenoid the output is assigned to on this vehicle.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: Safety monitor, wheel-speed calculation: speed value fails 0-1 m/s plausibility check
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 523100 (Safety monitor, wheel-speed calculation) with FMI 26 (Reserved by SAE; some OEMs assign proprietary meanings) is set by the ABS/ESC's internal safety-monitor software, which cross-checks stability-control functions -- wheel-speed math, roll/yaw control, brake blending, valve monitoring -- against each other and flags an inconsistency. WABCO is the OEM assigning this proprietary meaning to the FMI code here; diagnosis calls for a dealer-level scan tool, not a parts swap on the first visit.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: EEPROM parameter block 1 fails checksum verification, ECU may use a default value
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 524270 (EEPROM parameter block 1 checksum fault) with FMI 9 (Message not arriving at expected rate) is set by the ABS/ESC when a checksum on one of its stored EEPROM parameter groups -- traction control, brake configuration, gravity/vehicle setup, axle configuration -- fails, meaning the ECU's own configuration memory is corrupted. This is an internal ECU fault, not a wiring problem.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: EEPROM parameter block 2 fails checksum verification, ECU may use a default value
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 524271 (EEPROM parameter block 2 checksum fault) with FMI 19 (Network-received value flagged as error) is set by the ABS/ESC when a checksum on one of its stored EEPROM parameter groups -- traction control, brake configuration, gravity/vehicle setup, axle configuration -- fails, meaning the ECU's own configuration memory is corrupted. This is an internal ECU fault, not a wiring problem.
source_doc: MM1719 mBSP ABS/ESC maintenance manual (08.2018)

short_description: DEF quality sensor internal circuit shorted
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 3516 (DEF (urea) quality sensor, concentration error) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Aftertreatment DCU when the DEF quality (concentration) sensor reports an out-of-range reading, an optical/electrical fault, or a contaminated or wrong-type DEF condition. Wrong-strength or contaminated DEF is a real, common cause of this family, not just a sensor defect - check DEF concentration with a refractometer before replacing the sensor.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: DEF hose heater (back-flow/pressure/suction), H- or L-side shorted to battery
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 523557 (DEF hose heater, H-side circuit) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Aftertreatment DCU for one of the electric heater circuits on the DEF supply, return, suction or backflow hoses (open circuit, short to ground, short to battery, or critical overcurrent). These heaters keep DEF from freezing in the lines below ambient; a failed heater does not stop the truck from running but will set an inducement path if DEF cannot be pumped in cold weather.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: SCR downstream NOx sensor internal circuit shorted
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 523596 (SCR downstream NOx sensor internal circuit) with FMI 3 (Circuit voltage high / short to supply) is set by the Aftertreatment DCU for the NOx sensor mounted after the SCR catalyst (measuring tailpipe-out NOx to confirm conversion). The fault covers open/short circuits, communication loss, heater faults, offset/drift error, or the sensor reporting itself removed from the exhaust stream.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: Accelerator pedal position sensor circuit reads low (shorted to ground)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 91 (Accelerator pedal position sensor) with FMI 4 (Circuit voltage low / short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the accelerator pedal position sensor signal is missing, out of range or implausible relative to the engine's other timing references. Typical causes are a failed sensor, an incorrect air gap, connector corrosion, chafed wiring, or damage to the toothed wheel the sensor reads.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: ECU EEPROM memory fault
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 630 (Engine control module calibration/configuration fault) with FMI 2 (Signal unstable, intermittent or implausible) is set by the Engine ECU when it detects an internal fault in its own memory, software or supply. Typical causes are a corrupted calibration, a power/ground fault at the ECU connector, or, rarely, a failed ECU that needs dealer replacement and reprogramming.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: EGR valve actuator motor coil circuit open (disconnected)
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 2971 (EGR valve actuator motor coil circuit) with FMI 12 (Smart device or component defective) is set by the Engine ECU when the EGR valve actuator will not reach or hold a commanded position, reports an internal fault, loses calibration, or the motor coil circuit is open or shorted. Carbon buildup in the valve bore that increases actuator load is a leading mechanical cause behind an electrical-looking fault.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)

short_description: Buzzer output circuit shorted to battery supply
detailed_technical_explanation: SPN 518280 (Buzzer output circuit) with FMI 6 (Current too high; short to ground) is set by the Engine ECU when the dashboard warning lamp or indicator output circuit reads an abnormal voltage or current. Typical causes are a burned-out bulb/LED, a corroded connector, or a short/open in the wiring between the module and the indicator.
source_doc: Troubleshooting manual, engines over 56 kW (2024)
